screen.title: Calculations
screen.noGearSelected: Pick your gear to prefill the calculations

aperture.label: Aperture
aperture.description: Diameter of the lens or mirror

barlowFactor.label: Factor
barlowFactor.description: × for a Barlow, < 1 for a focal reducer

magnitudeDifference.label: Magnitude difference
magnitudeDifference.description: Difference between the two magnitudes (can be negative)

visualizations.sliderHint: Drag the marker to see the gear you'd need

moonField.moonWidthCount: The full Moon fits {{times}} times across it.

focalRatio.title: Focal ratio
focalRatio.formulaDescription: Describes how bright the instrument is: the smaller it is, the brighter the image and the wider the field.
focalRatio.resultNote: Below f/6: fast instrument, best for deep sky. Above f/9: better suited to planets/the Moon.

resolvingPower.title: Resolving power
resolvingPower.formulaDescription: Minimum angular gap (Dawes limit) between two points the instrument can distinguish.
resolvingPower.resultNote: Theoretical limit: atmospheric turbulence can degrade it in practice.

minMagnification.title: Minimum magnification
minMagnification.formulaDescription: Magnification below which the exit pupil exceeds 7 mm, the eye's maximum pupil size once dark-adapted: the image doesn't get any brighter beyond that.
minMagnification.resultNote: Below it, part of the light gathered by the instrument no longer enters the eye.

maxMagnification.title: Maximum magnification
maxMagnification.formulaDescription: Theoretical magnification beyond which atmospheric turbulence and diffraction prevent seeing more detail.
maxMagnification.resultNote: An absolute optical limit: actual seeing conditions often lower it well below this in practice.

barlowFocalLength.title: Focal length with Barlow/reducer
barlowFocalLength.formulaDescription: Focal length actually obtained by adding a Barlow (k > 1, e.g. 2×) or a focal reducer (k < 1, e.g. 0.8×) to the optical path.

limitingMagnitude.title: Limiting magnitude
limitingMagnitude.formulaDescription: Magnitude of the faintest star theoretically visible at the eyepiece, under a perfectly dark sky.
limitingMagnitude.resultNote: An optimistic estimate: light pollution, turbulence, the magnification used, and eye adaptation reduce it significantly in practice.

magnification.title: Magnification
magnification.formulaDescription: How many times larger the object appears compared to the naked eye.
magnification.usefulRange: Useful range of your instrument: {{min}}× to {{max}}×

low.label: Too low
low.note: Below the useful range: the image stays dim without showing more detail.

ideal.label: Useful
ideal.note: Magnification within the instrument's useful range.

high.label: Too high
high.note: Above the useful range: the image loses sharpness and brightness.

trueField.title: True field of view
trueField.formulaDescription: The portion of sky visible in the eyepiece.

exitPupil.title: Exit pupil
exitPupil.formulaDescription: Diameter of the light beam leaving the eyepiece, to compare with the eye's pupil (up to 7 mm in the dark).
exitPupil.resultNote: Above 7 mm, part of the light no longer enters the eye: the magnification is too low for the instrument.

sampling.title: Sampling
sampling.formulaDescription: The portion of sky covered by one camera pixel, in arcseconds. Only fill in a Barlow/reducer factor if you're using one: left blank, only the instrument's focal length counts.

fine.label: Fine
fine.note: Oversampled: only pays off with very stable skies and excellent tracking.

ideal.label: Balanced
ideal.note: Good compromise for most deep-sky targets.

wide.label: Wide field
wide.note: Undersampled: favours field of view over fine detail.

cameraField.title: Camera field of view
cameraField.formulaDescription: The portion of sky covered by the sensor, a rectangle, not a square: the headline result is the width, the height is used for the visualization's frame.

maxExposureTime.title: Max exposure time
maxExposureTime.formulaDescription: Maximum exposure time before star trailing from the sky's rotation becomes visible on a pixel (NPF rule).
maxExposureTime.resultNote: An approximation: actual trailing also depends on the target's declination and its distance from the celestial pole.

magnitudeConversion.title: Magnitude conversion
magnitudeConversion.formulaDescription: How many times brighter (or fainter) one object is than another, from the difference between their magnitudes.
magnitudeConversion.resultNote: A positive difference gives how many times fainter the second object is; negative, how many times brighter.
